_comment: Aura definitions. An aura is a field around a unit that affects other units by proximity. Any source may declare one with an `aura` key naming an id here: an item (passive_aura), a status (aura), a perk (aura), or a spell/active skill (aura, which applies its carrier status). Sources may override `magnitude` per instance — a graded item line does this to scale one aura across five consecrations. Resolution lives in scripts/combat/aura_system.gd; the vocabulary of payload kinds is enforced there, so a misspelled kind fails loudly instead of being silently skipped.
_comment_radius: Radius is in grid tiles, Chebyshev distance, and never includes the emitter unless `affects` is 'self' or 'all'.
_comment_affects: allies | enemies | all | self. `invert_for_enemies` flips the sign of every numeric payload for units on the other team, which is how one declaration expresses 'helps my side, hurts theirs'.

light_aura.name: Light of the Sun
light_aura._comment: Solar_Form declared this effect string for months with no consumer anywhere. Dazzling nearby enemies is the reading the status description already implied.

initiative_debuff.name: Weight of the Khatvanga
initiative_debuff._comment: Khatvanga items override the magnitude per consecration grade, -2 through -8.

avatar_of_the_storm.name: Avatar of the Storm
avatar_of_the_storm._comment: Party-wide rather than proximity-based, hence the radius. The air damage and stun chance this perk also grants stay in the on-hit path; only the standing bonus is an aura.

radiance_glare.name: Radiant Glare
radiance_glare._comment: The melee half of Radiance. Separate from the healing half because they reach different teams at different radii, which one aura cannot do.

radiant_visage.name: Radiant Visage
radiant_visage._comment: The spell described +2 AWR and +2 CON. Those are attributes, and an aura moves stats — so it grants what they would have bought: the initiative from Awareness and the health from Constitution.

shining_mirage.name: Shining Mirage
shining_mirage._comment: Battlefield-wide, and resistible. Each enemy who makes the save sees a little further through it, so the DC they personally face drops by 2 every time — the mirage wears out against anyone who keeps their head.
